name: inspect_region
description: Read a rectangle (max 45x45) as a compact token grid: what an object on each cell stands on. Use this before editing — do not guess current terrain.

name: get_objects
description: List placed objects (id, catalogId, position, rotation, elevation), at most 80 per call. Pass x1,y1,x2,y2 to list only objects placed in that rectangle, and category to list one catalog category.

name: get_catalog_item
description: Full catalog details for one item id (size, traits, display name, maxCount).

name: view_map
description: See the map as a rendered image (on vision models) or a token grid. Pass x1,y1,x2,y2 to view just that region, close up. Rendered images carry a coordinate ruler so you can map what you see to the cells you edit. Use it to judge COMPOSITION — shapes, balance, ragged edges — after major terrain or decoration work. The map shows what is built in its true colours; layer "plan" adds the planning annotations. layer "ground" shows the terrain alone, one colour per level, water by its level and every waterfall marked: the picture to judge levels, terraces and falls by, which the rendered map shows only as faint shades. Costs tokens on vision models; prefer evaluate_map for objective metrics.

layer.description: map (default): the rendered map as built, true colours. plan: the same with the planning annotations drawn over it. ground: the terrain alone by level.

name: place_object
description: Place a catalog item with its top-left anchor at (x,y). Ramps snap automatically — aim at a cliff-edge cell. BRIDGES: aim at a GAP cell (water/void, mid-channel) — use the anchors from find_bridge_sites. Returns the final (possibly snapped) placement.

name: remove_object
description: Remove a placed object by its id (from get_objects).

name: rotate_object
description: Rotate an existing rotatable object to an absolute rotation (re-validates placement).

name: find_flat_areas
description: Search the whole map for flat buildable spots where a footprint of minWidth x minHeight fits (grass zone, uniform elevation, no water, no objects; includes the +1 right/bottom margin the flat trait checks, so place_object at a returned anchor will pass). Pass catalogId (and rotation) to search for that item: its own turned footprint, beach as well where its groundZones allow it, and for a house the level ground its door side needs (V-PLACE-DOOR). Use this instead of guessing where things fit.

minWidth.description: Footprint width; taken from catalogId when given.

minHeight.description: Footprint height; taken from catalogId when given.

catalogId.description: The item to be placed: its footprint, ground zones and door decide the fit.

elevation.description: Terrain elevation to search on (default 0 = flat ground).

limit.description: Max anchors to return (default 5, spread apart).

name: check_build
description: Check what stands in the rectangle x1,y1,x2,y2 for faults a careful builder would fix, found by computation, not by looking: a door with no path, a path cut off or leading nowhere, water left in two pieces, sides meant to match that do not (objects, paving, water and raised ground alike), a row with uneven gaps, planting off-centre on its bed. Each finding names the cells. Call it once when a part is built, before you move on, while a fix is still one step.

name: carve_river
description: Carve a MEANDERING river through waypoints (a smooth curve through every waypoint, constant width, rounded banks): Smart Build's river. It runs downhill from its higher end, drops over a terrace step in a framed waterfall, and opens into a small pool at a dry end. Use 3-5 waypoints with sideways offsets for natural bends; straight 2-point calls are for canals. Banks stay bridgeable where the width is 3-6.

width.description: Channel width (default 4). An even width is centred on the waypoints' cells; an odd one lies half a cell up and left of them.

name: clear_area
description: Make room: in ONE step, remove every (non-locked) object touching the given cells AND erase the terrain under them back to flat grass. Use before reshaping an area instead of removing objects one by one. NEVER answer a refused placement by clearing a district you built — fix the exact cells instead. A clear removing more than 25 objects or covering more than 400 cells refuses unless demolish:true acknowledges the scale.

shape.description: Area form: "rect" fills x1,y1..x2,y2 (inclusive corners); "circle" fills radius r around cx,cy; "line" strokes x1,y1..x2,y2 at width; "cells" reads the cells array; "picture" reads a shape drawn as rows of text from x1,y1.

outline.description: With rect or circle: only the border cells (e.g. a mountain rim to contain water).

picture.description: For shape "picture": the shape drawn as rows of text, top row first, its top-left cell at x1,y1. "#" is a cell of the shape, "." is not. Draw any outline this way: a star, a letter, a crescent, an island with coves. Make the rows mirror images of themselves when the shape should be symmetric. Write a run of one mark as the mark and its count in braces: "#{12}.{4}" is twelve "#" then four ".".

scale.description: For shape "picture": how many cells each character stands for on a side (default 1). At 4 a row of 35 characters spans 140 cells, for outlines at island scale.

demolish.description: Acknowledge a large demolition (over 25 objects or 400 cells).

name: find_bridge_sites
description: Search for spots where a bridge can legally be placed (a straight gap of water/void/lower ground within the bridge's waterSpan, with flat EQUAL-height banks). Returns anchor cells you can pass directly to place_object. ALWAYS use this before placing a bridge — valid sites are rare and invisible in the token grid.

catalogId.description: Bridge item id (determines deck width); default bridge-plank.

name: find_ramp_sites
description: Scan for validated ramp placements connecting elevation tiers (the ramp equivalent of find_bridge_sites). Returns anchor cells, the catalog ramp item whose heightDrop matches each cliff, and which elevations it connects. Optional nearX/nearY and limit. Use before placing ramps instead of guessing cliff edges.

name: lay_route
description: Lay one path from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2) across whatever lies between, in one step: it climbs each change of level with a stair or ramp, crosses water with a bridge, goes round what stands in the way and meets standing pavement squarely. A point on a building means its door. It connects the two points or lays nothing and says where it stopped. Use it for each stretch of the main route, giving the places it should pass as the ends of successive calls, and for the path to each door, so that every level and every door is reached.

catalogId.description: The paving, a road id from the CATALOG (default: the map's main paving).

name: draw_area
description: Build a whole place from a drawing: rows of text, one character per cell, top-left at (x,y). Built-in marks: "." leaves the cell as it is, "~" water, a digit raised ground at that level (0 is flat ground, 1-9 higher). Every other character is defined in legend, one line each: "T=tree-apple", "p=path-stone", "h=house-id@90" (rotation), and "+" joins ground with things: "t=1+tree-apple" is a tree on level 1, "a=1+path-stone" paving on level 1. Ground is laid first, then paving, then everything else, in one undo step. A thing with no level of its own stands at the level of the ground drawn around it. Ground reaches half a cell past its marks. Whatever stands keeps its ground, so water drawn right beside a thing stops half a cell short of it and the thing stays on dry ground; water between two things needs two "~" across to show. Where two kinds of ground meet, the half cell between them goes to the one drawn less, the figure: a pool in a terrace or a shape of land in a pool keeps its drawn shape. A water body takes the level of the lowest ground around it, so a pool drawn on a terrace lies in the terrace. An item larger than one cell is one mark at its top-left cell, the rest of its footprint left "."; trees and houses need a free cell between them. mirror completes the drawing so both sides match exactly: "x" mirrors it to the right (draw the left half), "y" downward (draw the top half), "xy" both (draw the top-left quarter); give x2,y2, the far corner of the area, and draw the half rounded up: the tool completes it to exactly that size. repeatX and repeatY lay the finished drawing as a tile, gapX and gapY cells apart. scale draws ground at island size: each character stands for a square of that many cells on a side, so 35 characters span 140 cells; a drawing at a scale holds ground marks only, and x2,y2 stay in cells. The result counts what landed per mark and names what was refused.

reads_as.description: Before the rows: what a visitor must see here to call this place what was asked, and where this drawing puts each of it. A court is closed in on its sides, has a floor to stand on and one thing at its centre; an orchard is one tree in rows with lanes between; a word is letters a visitor can read, each one drawn as its letter. For a correction, what it restores.

x2.description: Right column the finished drawing must end on. With mirror "x" or "xy" draw the left half, rounded up: the tool completes it to exactly this width, sharing the middle column when the width is odd.

y2.description: Bottom row the finished drawing must end on; with mirror "y" or "xy" draw the top half, rounded up.

rows.description: The drawing, top row first; every row the same length. Write a run of one mark as the mark and its count in braces: "2{26}3{20}" is twenty-six 2s then twenty 3s.

legend.description: One line per mark you define: "<character>=<catalogId>", optionally "@<rotation>" and "<level>+" or "water+" before it. A mark may also be ground alone: "<character>=<level>" for land, "<character>=water<level>" for water held at that level, such as a pool raised on a terrace inside a ring of the terrace. A drawing does not make falls: unstated water touching lower ground is laid at the lower level, and water at a stated level must be ringed by ground of its own level; carve_river begun inside a raised pool makes the falls.

mirror.description: Complete the drawing by its mirror image: x to the right, y downward, xy both.

seam.description: Only without x2/y2. shared (default): the last column or row drawn is the middle, drawn once, for an odd size. doubled: it is repeated, for an even size.

replace.description: Remove what already stands on the cells that carry a mark before drawing (default false: occupied cells are skipped and reported).

scale.description: Cells each character stands for on a side (default 1). Above 1 the drawing holds ground only: digits, "~", "." and ground marks of the legend.

name: list_skills
description: List the available build playbooks (proven multi-step recipes for villages, hills, rivers…). Cheap — call it when the user asks for a composite scene.

name: load_skill
description: Load a technique or style reference from list_skills when relevant. Apply the parts that help the requested result; examples and optional features do not expand the task. Do not reload an already loaded skill.
